title: Building a 90s trading-card publisher sim with AI: what a human playtest caught
author: Little_Education_256
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/pr18wbij2v0i1.png

I'm developing Card Publisher Tycoon: The 90s Card Boom, a free management prototype in Unity. You compete for licences, design card sets, choose print runs and prices, and try to keep your publishing company afloat during 1995–2000. It's playable in the browser and on Windows, in English and French.



AI tools have been used extensively for programming, card illustrations, in-game text and translation. My work is choosing the direction, reviewing and revising the results, and deciding what belongs in the game. The card art went through many iterations to get closer to the look of printed 90s cards. Nothing is generated live during play.



The most useful recent feedback came from a 30-minute human playtest. The tester understood the guided opening, but later lost track of a pending licence bid and wasn't sure how to interpret the requirements. They also struggled with the early economy. That led to clearer bid requirements and bid tracking, followed by another balance pass.



The latest build adds a permanent card album, three different starts per scenario, optional alternate-history trends and rivals that improve over time. One design choice I'm keeping is experimentation: the player should work out a profitable recipe rather than be handed one.



For me, getting the systems implemented and checking their rules hasn't answered whether the decisions are readable or interesting. Watching someone play has been a useful separate step. How do you test that gap in your AI-assisted projects?



Free prototype: [https://mgeoff1.itch.io/tcg-publisher-tycoon](https://mgeoff1.itch.io/tcg-publisher-tycoon)

Please start a new game after updating.
